key_insight: LLM agents often fail to execute the planning structure they declare, so reliable long-horizon performance depends on both choosing the right planning mode and faithfully routing execution to it.
engineering_relevance: For agent builders, the main design lesson is to separate mode selection from execution and use pattern-specific executors to reduce planning-to-execution drift.
method: Study the Plan Declaration–Execution Gap in LLM agents
Compare generic Plan+ReAct with Planning-as-Routing across four planning modes: Predefined, Sequential, Hierarchical, and Search
Evaluate plan-structure preservation and task success across four benchmarks and three LLMs
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks and three LLMs, generic Plan+ReAct preserved declared planning structure only 22%–45% of the time on three benchmarks, while routing improved success from 0.48 to 0.92 on ALFWorld and from 0.36 to 0.44 on SWE-bench Verified.
watch_item: Mode selection is still unreliable: current LLMs do not consistently choose the strongest planning mode for each task, so routing helps execution but does not solve planning-choice errors.
paper_title: Do LLM Agents Execute the Plans They Declare? From Planning-Mode Declaration to Pattern-Specific Execution
